edge_explainer: Unlike ACSO the shelf row is ACCURATE - 2.3x EV/EBIT, $61.7m net cash and zero capital commitments are all CONFIRMED against primaries (TTM EBIT $84,728k reconstructed as FY25 $68,245k + Q1-26 $27,097k - Q1-25 $10,614k, matching the row exactly; AR2025 Note 23 verbatim: 'At 31 December 2025 the Group has not made any commitments for capital purchases'). The problem is not the data, it is that the denominator is a gold price. Commodity frame test: the premise 'gold at ATH = peak earnings' is HALF REFUTED - gold has ALREADY rolled over, live spot $4,094.6 is ~15% BELOW the $4,826/oz Serabi realised in the quarter that anchors the trailing multiple. The real trap is the cost side: AISC has ratcheted $1,326 (2023) to $1,700 to $1,816 to $2,293 (Q1-26), +73%, with the BRL STRENGTHENING (5.85 to 5.26/USD) so FX is a headwind not a cushion. Cost ratchets in underground mining do not reverse, so a gold reversion lands on a much higher floor: at $2,400 gold AISC eats ~96% of the price. Normalised deck at AISC $2,293: 2.3x becomes 7.1x-8.2x at $2,800 gold and 33x-39x at $2,400 - so NO, 2.3x does not survive the requested deck. But the honest full answer has three parts: at the company's OWN long-term assumption of $3,500/oz (AR2025 going-concern note) it is 3.0-3.4x and still cheap, and at live spot it is 2.0-2.3x and real, because the volume ramp offsets margin compression. The market is not mispricing Serabi; it is pricing a gold reversion and is right to. Therefore RISK_PREMIUM, never EDGE - we would be buying an unhedged gold distribution on which this desk has no view. MODE B found the item the shelf never saw: 62% of production (Coringa, 7,450 of 12,043 oz in Q1-26) runs on a THREE-YEAR TRIAL 'GUIA' licence with the full Installation Licence still PENDING and the process involving indigenous groups; management asserts to its auditors that it 'will be resolved' - a management judgement, not an obtained permit. Production is also behind: H1-26 23,050 oz annualises to ~46koz vs a 53-57koz guide, requiring +36% above the Q2 rate. Tails are bounded though: debt-free, no warrants, no dilution across three balance-sheet dates, and net cash of 60p/share = 24% of the price.
